title: Federal Agency Mail Management Act of 2017
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was introduced. The expanded summary of the House reported version is repeated here.)

Federal Agency Mail Management Act of 2017

(Sec. 2) This bill amends the Presidential and Federal Records Act Amendments of 2014 to require the General Services Administration (GSA) to provide guidance and assistance to federal agencies for effective mail processing.

The GSA: (1) must promote economy and efficiency in the selection and utilization of space, staff, equipment, and supplies for federal mail processing facilities; and (2) may inspect the mail processing practices and programs of federal agencies for purposes of recommending improvements.

The bill also provides authority for the GSA to set goals for the establishment and maintenance of federal records management systems or techniques.

summary.headline: This law directs the General Services Administration to help federal agencies run their mail operations more efficiently and to review their mail practices.
summary.what_it_does: The law changes the Presidential and Federal Records Act Amendments of 2014. It requires the General Services Administration (GSA) to give federal agencies guidance and help with processing mail. The GSA must promote economy and efficiency in how agencies choose and use space, staff, equipment, and supplies for mail facilities. The GSA may also inspect agency mail practices and suggest improvements, and it can set goals for federal records management systems.

who_it_affects.how: They must receive GSA guidance and assistance on mail processing and may have their mail practices inspected with recommendations for improvement.
The agency is required to provide mail processing guidance and gains authority to review agency mail practices and set records management goals.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was enacted on November 21, 2017.
